changelog.name: Solid ground
changes: SIM phase 1: the battlefield. Every map, its terrain and pathfinding now work in Godot exactly as in the web game (checked against recordings of web v22.5).
Exact maths (sim/dmath.gd): sin, cos, atan2, pow, hypot and round give the browser's results bit for bit, on every OS, so battles match the web game and stay in sync between players later.
Maps: all 20 fixed maps in data/maps.json; Chaos Isles rolls the same map as the web game for the same seed.

Terrain: heights, coastlines, coves, base pads, walkable ground, boat water and scattered rocks, ruins and wrecks are identical to the web game on all 18 land maps, a team battle and two Chaos battles.
Pathfinding finds the same routes as the web game (400 recorded paths), plus the spatial lookup units use to find each other, and the unit, base and facility tables.
Army profiles moved to data/factions.json; map-building numbers to data/mapgen.json.
Under the hood: Godot's JSON reader and Vector2 lose precision, so long numbers are stored exactly and the SIM never uses Godot vectors. A test that crashes now counts as a failure.

changelog.name: Baseline v22.5
changes: The port now follows web v22.5, which stays frozen until the port is done (the web reference copy is web/dawgs_uprising_v22.5.html).
Balance from v22.4: the light tank fires the new heavy machine gun (weapon 'hmg'); its damage, fire rate and accuracy changed to match.
Web comparison recordings re-made from v22.5. v22.5 itself only changed camera controls, which the renderer port will pick up.
Tests run from the editor now stay open and show every result in their window (the Output panel could miss the last lines when the run quit straight away).

changelog.name: Skeleton
changes: Godot 4.7.2 project with the web version's split: sim/ (pure logic), render/ (battle view and HUD), menus/.
Every BALANCE number from web v22.3 is in data/balance.json.
The SIM runs a fixed 1/30 s step like the web game; the battle screen shows its clock. No units yet.
First SIM piece: the seeded random generator (sim/rng.gd), checked number-for-number against the web game. The tests compare the port with recordings of the web SIM in tests/golden/.
